Come join Analog Devices (ADI) – a place where Innovation meets Impact. For more than 55 years, Analog Devices has been inventing new breakthrough technologies that transform lives. At ADI you will work alongside the brightest minds to collaborate on solving complex problems that matter from autonomous vehicles, drones and factories to augmented reality and remote healthcare.

About Analog Devices

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.

          

Analog Devices is seeking a Field Robotics Systems Engineer to help develop, integrate, and demonstrate next-generation robotic systems and intelligent machines. 

As part of the Robotics Systems and Platform team, you will work across robotics hardware, embedded software, perception, motion control, AI, and system integration to create proof-of-concepts (PoCs), demonstrations, and customer-facing solutions that showcase the value of ADI technology. 

Working alongside experienced engineers and robotics experts, you will gain hands-on experience supporting customers from early technology evaluations through system integration and validation. This role provides an opportunity to apply academic knowledge to real-world robotics challenges while contributing to innovative solutions spanning industrial robotics, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robotics, and service robotics. 

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

Design, build, and integrate proof-of-concepts (PoCs), demonstrations, and reference systems for robotics applications.
Work hands-on with robotic subsystems including sensing, perception, motion control, embedded computing, power systems, and AI-enabled technologies.
Support system bring-up, integration, testing, debugging, and validation across hardware and software domains.
Develop robotics applications using tools and frameworks such as Python, C/C++, ROS2, Linux, Isaac Sim, Gazebo, and CodeFusion Studio.
Create and evaluate robotic solutions in simulation and digital twin environments and support deployment to physical robotic platforms.
Collaborate with customers, ecosystem partners, and internal ADI teams to develop system-level robotics solutions.
Support customer workshops, demonstrations, technical evaluations, and co-creation activities through ADI Catalyst and other innovation programs.
Participate in technical forums, industry events, and customer engagements to showcase ADI technologies.
Contribute to reusable platforms, reference designs, technical documentation, and demonstration assets that accelerate customer adoption.

Minimum Qualifications 

B.S. in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Engineering.
Academic, internship, research, or project experience building, integrating, or testing robotic systems or mechatronic platforms.
Familiarity with electronic hardware, schematics, and test equipment (scopes, logic analyzers)
Foundational knowledge of robotics technologies, including one or more of the following:
Motion control and actuation
Robotic sensing and perception
Sensor fusion
Embedded and real-time systems
Autonomous robotic systems
Experience with robotics software development using Python and/or C/C++.
Familiarity with Linux and robotics frameworks such as ROS or ROS2.
Experience with simulation tools such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo, RoboDK, or MATLAB/Simulink.
Exposure to AI/ML, computer vision, perception systems, or autonomous robotics through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects.
Strong problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.

Preferred Qualifications 

M.S. in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Engineering.
Experience with advanced robotic systems such as industrial robots, AMRs, humanoids, collaborative robots, or robotic manipulation systems.
Expertise in electronic hardware design, testing, and troubleshooting to the component level.
Experience with perception technologies including computer vision, depth sensing, VSLAM, force/torque sensing, audio sensing, or multi-sensor fusion.
Familiarity with robotics compute platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson Nano, Orin NX, and Orin AGX.
Implementation of AI/ML, Physical AI, robotic perception, or autonomous systems.
Experience developing robotics demonstrations, capstone projects, research platforms, or proof-of-concepts.
Participation in robotics competitions, university design teams, research programs, or open-source robotics initiatives.
Interest in customer engagement, technical workshops, and emerging robotics ecosystems.

Core Technical Areas 

Successful candidates will have experience or interest in developing expertise in: 

Robotics Systems and Hardware
Robotics Frameworks and Embedded Software
Simulation and Digital Twin Tools
Motion Control, Perception, and Sensor Fusion
Robotics and Mechatronics Integration

The expected wage range for a new hire into this position is $87,188 to $119,906.

Actual wage offered may vary depending on work location, experience, education, training, external market data, internal pay equity, or other bona fide factors.

This position qualifies for a discretionary performance-based bonus which is based on personal and company factors.

This position includes medical, vision and dental coverage, 401k, paid vacation, holidays, and sick time, and other benefits.
